lines.raw: Lesson 2: Medical Claim Types.
lines.say: Lesson 2: Medical Claim Types.

lines.raw: In the US, the doctor and the hospital usually send separate bills.
lines.say: In the U S, the doctor and the hospital usually send separate bills.

lines.raw: In this lesson you will:
lines.say: In this lesson you will:

lines.raw: Tell the difference between a professional claim and an institutional claim.
lines.say: Tell the difference between a professional claim and an institutional claim.

lines.raw: See how one emergency room visit creates a hospital claim and a doctor claim.
lines.say: See how one emergency room visit creates a hospital claim and a doctor claim.

lines.raw: Know which fields appear only on institutional or only on professional claims.
lines.say: Know which fields appear only on institutional or only on professional claims.

lines.raw: Understand inpatient vs. outpatient.
lines.say: Understand inpatient versus outpatient.

lines.raw: Doctor's work vs. hospital's building.
lines.say: Doctor's work versus hospital's building.

lines.raw: When you are treated in a hospital, two different things are being "used": the **skills of the doctor** and the **hospital itself**: its bed, emergency room, nurses, machines and supplies.
lines.say: When you are treated in a hospital, two different things are being "used": the skills of the doctor and the hospital itself: its bed, emergency room, nurses, machines and supplies.

lines.raw: Think of a wedding party venue.
lines.say: Think of a wedding party venue.

lines.raw: You rent a party palace (the building, chairs, kitchen) and separately hire a photographer.
lines.say: You rent a party palace (the building, chairs, kitchen) and separately hire a photographer.

lines.raw: The party palace sends one bill, the photographer sends another.
lines.say: The party palace sends one bill, the photographer sends another.

lines.raw: In US healthcare, the **hospital is the party palace** (institutional claim), and the **doctor is the photographer** (professional claim).
lines.say: In U S healthcare, the hospital is the party palace (institutional claim), and the doctor is the photographer (professional claim).

lines.raw: The idea in one sentence: **a professional claim bills for a person's work, and an institutional claim bills for a facility's services.**
lines.say: The idea in one sentence: a professional claim bills for a person's work, and an institutional claim bills for a facility's services.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Bills for. Professional claim: A person's work (doctor, nurse practitioner, therapist). Institutional claim: A facility's services (hospital, nursing home).
lines.say: Bills for. Professional claim: A person's work (doctor, nurse practitioner, therapist). Institutional claim: A facility's services (hospital, nursing home).

lines.raw: Paper form. Professional claim: **CMS-1500** (named after CMS, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the US government's health agency). Institutional claim: **UB-04** (also called CMS-1450).
lines.say: Paper form. Professional claim: C M S 1500 (named after C M S, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, the U S government's health agency). Institutional claim: U B 04 (also called C M S 1450).

lines.raw: Electronic format. Professional claim: **837P** (P = Professional). Institutional claim: **837I** (I = Institutional).
lines.say: Electronic format. Professional claim: 8 3 7 P (P = Professional). Institutional claim: 8 3 7 I (I = Institutional).

lines.raw: Example. Professional claim: The ER doctor's fee for examining the patient. Institutional claim: The ER room, nurses, X-ray machine, supplies.
lines.say: Example. Professional claim: The E R doctor's fee for examining the patient. Institutional claim: The E R room, nurses, X-ray machine, supplies.

lines.raw: Often called. Professional claim: "Doctor claim", "physician claim". Institutional claim: "Facility claim", "hospital claim".
lines.say: Often called. Professional claim: "Doctor claim", "physician claim". Institutional claim: "Facility claim", "hospital claim".

lines.raw: One ER visit, two claims.
lines.say: One E R visit, two claims.

lines.raw: In Nepal: A night in the emergency room in Kathmandu.
lines.say: In Nepal: A night in the emergency room in Kathmandu.

lines.raw: With private insurance:
lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: Ram falls off his scooter and hurts his wrist.
lines.say: Ram falls off his scooter and hurts his wrist.

lines.raw: He goes to a private hospital's **emergency** at night.
lines.say: He goes to a private hospital's emergency at night.

lines.raw: He gets **one final bill**, but it lists separate items: **emergency charge**, **doctor fee**, **X-ray**, **plaster**.
lines.say: He gets one final bill, but it lists separate items: emergency charge, doctor fee, X-ray, plaster.

lines.raw: He pays at the counter, then sends the bill to his insurer to be reimbursed.
lines.say: He pays at the counter, then sends the bill to his insurer to be reimbursed.

lines.raw: Nepal combines everything in one bill.
lines.say: Nepal combines everything in one bill.

lines.raw: The US splits the doctor's fee and the hospital's charges into different claims.
lines.say: The U S splits the doctor's fee and the hospital's charges into different claims.

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: Sita has the same fall and goes to an SSF-listed hospital's emergency.
lines.say: Sita has the same fall and goes to an S S F listed hospital's emergency.

lines.raw: The hospital sends SSF **one claim** for the whole visit: emergency charge, doctor, X-ray and plaster.
lines.say: The hospital sends S S F one claim for the whole visit: emergency charge, doctor, X-ray and plaster.

lines.raw: In the US: Emily's ER visit creates two claims.
lines.say: In the U S: Emily's E R visit creates two claims.

lines.raw: Emily twists her wrist and goes to the **emergency room (ER)** at Lakeside General Hospital.
lines.say: Emily twists her wrist and goes to the emergency room (E R) at Lakeside General Hospital.

lines.raw: She is X-rayed, splinted and sent home the same night.
lines.say: She is X-rayed, splinted and sent home the same night.

lines.raw: **Hospital claim → UB-04 / 837I**: the ER room and nursing, the X-ray picture, the splint.
lines.say: Hospital claim to U B 04 or 8 3 7 I: the E R room and nursing, the X-ray picture, the splint.

lines.raw: Billing provider: Lakeside General Hospital.
lines.say: Billing provider: Lakeside General Hospital.

lines.raw: **Doctor claim → CMS-1500 / 837P**: the ER doctor's examination.
lines.say: Doctor claim to C M S 1500 or 8 3 7 P: the E R doctor's examination.

lines.raw: Billing provider: the ER doctors' group, not the hospital.
lines.say: Billing provider: the E R doctors' group, not the hospital.

lines.raw: Both go to the same insurance company, often on different days.
lines.say: Both go to the same insurance company, often on different days.

lines.raw: Emily's ER visit as two claims.
lines.say: Emily's E R visit as two claims.

lines.raw: Claim type. Claim 1: hospital: Institutional. Claim 2: ER doctor: Professional.
lines.say: Claim type. Claim 1: hospital: Institutional. Claim 2: E R doctor: Professional.

lines.raw: Form. Claim 1: hospital: UB-04 / 837I. Claim 2: ER doctor: CMS-1500 / 837P.
lines.say: Form. Claim 1: hospital: U B 04 or 8 3 7 I. Claim 2: E R doctor: C M S 1500 or 8 3 7 P.

lines.raw: Who gets paid. Claim 1: hospital: Lakeside General Hospital. Claim 2: ER doctor: Lakeside Emergency Physicians (the doctors' group).
lines.say: Who gets paid. Claim 1: hospital: Lakeside General Hospital. Claim 2: E R doctor: Lakeside Emergency Physicians (the doctors' group).

lines.raw: What it bills. Claim 1: hospital: ER room, nursing, X-ray picture, splint. Claim 2: ER doctor: The doctor's examination and treatment.
lines.say: What it bills. Claim 1: hospital: E R room, nursing, X-ray picture, splint. Claim 2: E R doctor: The doctor's examination and treatment.

lines.raw: Billed. Claim 1: hospital: $1,400. Claim 2: ER doctor: $350.
lines.say: Billed. Claim 1: hospital: 1400 dollars. Claim 2: E R doctor: 350 dollars.

lines.raw: Common beginner mistake.
lines.say: Common beginner mistake.

lines.raw: One visit can produce several claims from different providers.
lines.say: One visit can produce several claims from different providers.

lines.raw: A hospital stay with surgery often makes three or more: the hospital, the surgeon and the anaesthesiologist.
lines.say: A hospital stay with surgery often makes three or more: the hospital, the surgeon and the anaesthesiologist.

lines.raw: If you want the full cost of Emily's ER visit, you must add up the hospital claim **and** the doctor claim for that date.
lines.say: If you want the full cost of Emily's E R visit, you must add up the hospital claim and the doctor claim for that date.

lines.raw: Inpatient vs. outpatient.
lines.say: Inpatient versus outpatient.

lines.raw: Inpatient.
lines.say: Inpatient.

lines.raw: The patient is formally **admitted** and stays overnight (usually at least one night).
lines.say: The patient is formally admitted and stays overnight (usually at least one night).

lines.raw: In Nepal: being "admitted to the ward" or "bharna".
lines.say: In Nepal: being "admitted to the ward" or "bharna".

lines.raw: Outpatient.
lines.say: Outpatient.

lines.raw: The patient comes and goes without being admitted.
lines.say: The patient comes and goes without being admitted.

lines.raw: In Nepal: **OPD** visits, day-care procedures, X-rays, tests.
lines.say: In Nepal: O P D visits, day-care procedures, X-rays, tests.

lines.raw: Emily's ER visit is outpatient: she went home the same night.
lines.say: Emily's E R visit is outpatient: she went home the same night.

lines.raw: Common claim categories you will see in data.
lines.say: Common claim categories you will see in data.

lines.raw: Inpatient facility. Form: UB-04 / 837I. Example: Hospital stay for surgery, childbirth, pneumonia.
lines.say: Inpatient facility. Form: U B 04 or 8 3 7 I. Example: Hospital stay for surgery, childbirth, pneumonia.

lines.raw: Outpatient facility. Form: UB-04 / 837I. Example: Hospital ER visit, day surgery, CT scan at hospital.
lines.say: Outpatient facility. Form: U B 04 or 8 3 7 I. Example: Hospital E R visit, day surgery, C T scan at hospital.

lines.raw: Professional. Form: CMS-1500 / 837P. Example: Doctor visit, surgeon fee, physiotherapy session.
lines.say: Professional. Form: C M S 1500 or 8 3 7 P. Example: Doctor visit, surgeon fee, physiotherapy session.

lines.raw: Pharmacy. Form: NCPDP (separate format). Example: Medicines from a pharmacy (see the Pharmacy course).
lines.say: Pharmacy. Form: N C P D P (separate format). Example: Medicines from a pharmacy (see the Pharmacy course).

lines.raw: Other. Form: Varies. Example: Ambulance, wheelchair, dental, vision.
lines.say: Other. Form: Varies. Example: Ambulance, wheelchair, dental, vision.

lines.raw: Which fields belong to which claim type?
lines.say: Which fields belong to which claim type?

scenes.section: Which fields belong to which claim type?

lines.raw: Most fields appear on both claim types: member, claim number, billing provider, diagnoses, procedure codes, dates and amounts.
lines.say: Most fields appear on both claim types: member, claim number, billing provider, diagnoses, procedure codes, dates and amounts.

lines.raw: A few appear on **only one** type.
lines.say: A few appear on only one type.

lines.raw: You do not need to know these fields yet; later lessons explain each one.
lines.say: You do not need to know these fields yet; later lessons explain each one.

lines.raw: Just notice that the two types are shaped differently.
lines.say: Just notice that the two types are shaped differently.

scenes.section: Which fields belong to which claim type?

lines.raw: Side by side: fields that only one claim type has.
lines.say: Side by side: fields that only one claim type has.

lines.raw: **Type of Bill**: what kind of facility bill this is, e.g. hospital inpatient (lesson 9). Professional only (CMS-1500): **Place of Service**: where the doctor gave the care, e.g. office or ER (lesson 9).
lines.say: Type of Bill: what kind of facility bill this is, for example hospital inpatient (lesson 9). Professional only (C M S 1500): Place of Service: where the doctor gave the care, for example office or E R (lesson 9).

lines.raw: **Revenue code** on each line: which hospital department the charge belongs to (lesson 9). Professional only (CMS-1500): **Diagnosis pointer** on each line: which diagnosis supports that line (lesson 5).
lines.say: Revenue code on each line: which hospital department the charge belongs to (lesson 9). Professional only (C M S 1500): Diagnosis pointer on each line: which diagnosis supports that line (lesson 5).

lines.raw: **Admission and discharge dates** for inpatient stays (lesson 7). Professional only (CMS-1500): A **rendering provider** filled on every line, naming the doctor who did the work (on hospital claims it is often empty) (lesson 8).
lines.say: Admission and discharge dates for inpatient stays (lesson 7). Professional only (C M S 1500): A rendering provider filled on every line, naming the doctor who did the work (on hospital claims it is often empty) (lesson 8).

lines.raw: **Admitting diagnosis** and **Present on Admission** flags for inpatient stays (lesson 5).
lines.say: Admitting diagnosis and Present on Admission flags for inpatient stays (lesson 5).

lines.raw: **Attending provider**: the main doctor responsible for a hospital stay (lesson 8).
lines.say: Attending provider: the main doctor responsible for a hospital stay (lesson 8).

lines.raw: **ICD-10-PCS** procedure codes for inpatient stays (lesson 6).
lines.say: I C D 10-PCS procedure codes for inpatient stays (lesson 6).

lines.raw: **DRG**: the package group for an inpatient stay (lesson 10).
lines.say: D R G: the package group for an inpatient stay (lesson 10).

lines.raw: Why this matters for data.
lines.say: Why this matters for data.

lines.raw: Most data teams load both types into **one claim table** with a `claim_type` column (Institutional / Professional, sometimes stored as `I` / `P`).
lines.say: Most data teams load both types into one claim table with a claim_type column (Institutional or Professional, sometimes stored as I or P).

lines.raw: The fields that do not apply to a row are left empty (**NULL**).
lines.say: The fields that do not apply to a row are left empty (N U L L).

lines.raw: Always filter or group on `claim_type` before comparing hospitals with doctors, or you will mix apples and oranges.
lines.say: Always filter or group on claim_type before comparing hospitals with doctors, or you will mix apples and oranges.

lines.raw: Paper forms and electronic files.
lines.say: Paper forms and electronic files.

lines.raw: The **CMS-1500** and **UB-04** are paper forms with numbered boxes.
lines.say: The C M S 1500 and U B 04 are paper forms with numbered boxes.

lines.raw: Today, almost all claims are sent **electronically** as text files in a format called **X12 837**.
lines.say: Today, almost all claims are sent electronically as text files in a format called X12 8 37.

lines.raw: The boxes on the paper form map to fields in the file.
lines.say: The boxes on the paper form map to fields in the file.

lines.raw: How these standard files work is covered in the Interoperability course.
lines.say: How these standard files work is covered in the Interoperability course.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: **Professional** claims bill for a person's work: CMS-1500 on paper, 837P electronically.
lines.say: Professional claims bill for a person's work: C M S 1500 on paper, 8 3 7 P electronically.

lines.raw: **Institutional** claims bill for a facility: UB-04 on paper, 837I electronically.
lines.say: Institutional claims bill for a facility: U B 04 on paper, 8 3 7 I electronically.

lines.raw: One ER visit usually creates a hospital claim plus a doctor claim; a hospital stay creates even more.
lines.say: One E R visit usually creates a hospital claim plus a doctor claim; a hospital stay creates even more.

lines.raw: Some fields exist on only one type (Type of Bill and revenue codes on institutional; Place of Service on professional).
lines.say: Some fields exist on only one type (Type of Bill and revenue codes on institutional; Place of Service on professional).

lines.raw: In a combined table they are NULL on the other type.
lines.say: In a combined table they are N U L L on the other type.
